name: old cracked asphalt road of warm charcoal grey: a five-step grey ramp of small worn grain clumps, clustered 2-3 pixel light aggregate flecks and a few shaded 2-pixel-wide fractures (no lane paint), its unconnected edges broken off into dirt with bitten-out gaps and loose 3x2 asphalt chunks and a dry dark-brown ledge on the south side, laid as a road network with crossroads, dead ends and long straight runs that mix three edge variants
label: wasteland_ruins/asphalt

surfaces.part: asphalt road network patches on dirt ground

answer.evidence: The image is a flat terrain tileset sheet (288x240) showing brown dirt ground with grey cracked asphalt road pieces: crossroads, T-junctions, dead ends, a large square block and long straight runs. Everything is drawn as a flat ground surface seen from above, with no standing volume, no front face and no eave or edge line. The dark ledge on the south side is only a thin edge shading, not a vertical face of 3 or more rows. The kind is terrain, so it matches, and the sheet reads as flat ground, not a standing object.

styleAnswer.evidence: Both the asphalt and the dirt carry dense grain, with light aggregate flecks on the grey and mottled clumps on the brown, so no area reads as a flat fill. Near-flat coverage is 3%, close to the references' 0%. The asphalt shows about 4-5 grey steps (dark base, mid clumps, light flecks, shaded fractures), and the dirt about 3 browns, close to Beodeul's 5-6 per material. Visible tones per tile are 5, above the grass reference (3) and a little below the paving reference (7), so density is slightly lower but acceptable. Only 32% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the edges lean toward tinted dark grey and brown rather than a uniform black sticker outline. The bitten, irregular edges and loose chunks are separated mostly by value. The palette is small at 10 colours in total, which is a mild weakness against the richer paving reference, but the visible craft holds up next to the references.
